test: the welcome page names Kothari's and says what TableTurn is
what_should_happen: When the app opens on the welcome page, a small line names the restaurant and where it is. The big heading reads "Twenty-two tables." with "No wipe-clean board." on its second line, and the paragraph under it starts with the words about an honest wait.
exact_words: Every party gets a place in the queue and an honest wait

test: on a fresh evening the counts read 22 tables, 22 free right now and 0 in use
what_should_happen: On a fresh evening nobody has been seated. Once the welcome page has read the floor, its three counts read 22 tables, 22 free right now and 0 in use.

test: with one table seated and another waiting to be cleared, free right now shows 20 and in use shows 2
what_should_happen: Before the page opens, one party sits at a table and another party has left its table, which nobody has wiped yet. The counts come from the real floor, so 20 tables are free right now and 2 are in use, out of 22.

test: the drawing shows the table tops T01 to T04, T11 to T13 and T19, and no other table
what_should_happen: The small drawing beside the heading shows exactly eight table tops from the real floor. They are T01 to T04, T11 to T13 and T19, and no other table number appears on the page.

test: the drawing is only a picture: clicking a table top does nothing
what_should_happen: Clicking a table top in the drawing does nothing. The address stays on the welcome page and no panel opens.

reason: Whether each table top in the drawing looks free, seated or to be cleared is a colour and a drawing, and the drawing is hidden from screen readers.

test: before the floor is read the counts show 0 and the drawing is empty, then both fill in
what_should_happen: In the first moment, before the floor has been read, the counts show 0 and the drawing has no table tops. A moment later both fill in by themselves, with no reload: 22 tables, 22 free right now, and the table tops appear.

test: under "Who are you today?" there is one card each for Meera, Joseph, a guest and Ravi
what_should_happen: Under "Who are you today?" a line says that each person sees their own screens and changes the same floor. There are four cards, Meera the host, Joseph on the floor, a guest and Ravi the manager, each with its one-line description and "Continue as" with the person.
exact_words: Each person sees their own screens. Everything they do changes the same floor.
Runs the host stand. Sees every table, keeps the waitlist and seats each party.
Works the floor. Marks a table when the party leaves, and again once it is wiped.
Gives a name at the stand. Sees the wait they were quoted and, once seated, the wait they had.
Owns the restaurant. Reads every party’s record.
